newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau, China police promise more cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Macau, China police promise more cooperation.

text.p: Police officials from China and the Portuguese-administered enclave of Macau agreed on Monday to strengthen cooperation in the fight against cross-border crime.

Zhu Mingjian, vice-director of the Guangdong Provincial Public Securitiy Bureau, said after a meeting with his Macanese counterpart that both sides had agreed to strengthen cooperation to combat organised crime, drugs and smuggling.
Carlos Cardoso, commander of the Macau Marine Police, described the meeting as "very helpful".

Tiny Macau, a territory of 455,000 people perched on China's southern coast, has recently been hit with a surge in violent crime linked to a turf war between rival "triad" gangs, with 15 murders so far this year versus 21 for the whole of 1996.
The territory shares a 240-metre land border with China. Macau police believe many crimes in the enclave are committed by mainland Chinese, who flee back into China minutes later.
